statement.summary: Proposition 9.2 is split into five Props conjoined in `propDetectAvgStatement`: (i) `detectAvgOrbitsStatement` — the exact uniform average of the number of orbits visited by the stand-alone test of ⟨w⟩ (any p | n prime, any generator w of order p, any traversal order, both readings) is (1 − Q^m)/(1 − Q); (ii) `detectAvgReadsStatement` — the uniform average of `detect`'s reads is ≤ Σ_{p|n} [d 1]_p p/(1 − σ^{1−p}); (iii) `detectAvgBoundLeStatement` — the middle inequality; (iv) `detectAvgBigOStatement` — the O-claim as ∃ C uniform in n, d; (v) `detectAvgReadsBigOStatement` — the composed bound with one constant. The expectation is the explicit average `expectUnif` over all σ^{n^d} configurations.
deltas: Expectation under the uniform distribution = `expectUnif f = (Σ_s f s) / |Fin σ^{Lat n d}|`, in ℝ.
Q = σ^{1−p} is the integer power `(σ : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℤ) − p)` (no truncation); 1 − Q ≠ 0 since σ, p ≥ 2.
m = N/p is ℕ-division `n ^ d / p`, exact because p | n | n^d.
'The test of a single order-p subgroup, run on its own' = `subgroupTest stopEarly s ord p w` with its second component (orbits visited, the failing orbit included).
The subgroup is given by any generator w with `addOrderOf w = p` (every order-p subgroup with every choice of generator).
'The full algorithm' = `detect` over any schedule, any per-subgroup traversal orders, both readings (see Theorem 9.1's mapping for the algorithm model).
'= O(Σ_{p|n} p^d)' is the one-sided Landau bound with one constant C uniform in n and d (d is part of the input); (v) also uniform in σ.
Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 explicit; `[NeZero n]` only supplies the Fintype instance.

tex.text: For $\ssb$ uniform on $\Sigma^{n^d}$, the test of any single order-$p$ subgroup, run on its own, visits in expectation exactly $\frac{1-Q^{m}}{1-Q}$ orbits, with $Q=\sigma^{1-p}$ and $m=N/p$. Consequently, the expected total number of cells read by the full algorithm is at most

lean.text:
detectAvgOrbitsStatement n d σ ∧ detectAvgReadsStatement n d σ ∧
    detectAvgBoundLeStatement n d σ ∧ detectAvgBigOStatement ∧
    detectAvgReadsBigOStatement

maps.note: Parts (i)–(v).

maps.label: the algorithm of §9 = `detect`

tex.text: \textbf{Algorithm.} For each prime $p\mid n$ and each of the $\gaussbinom d1_p$ order-$p$ cyclic subgroups $C=\langle\ww\rangle$ (enumerated via one representative line each, Lemma~\ref{lem:torsion}): traverse the cells in a fixed order (which may depend on the subgroup); for each yet-unvisited cell, walk its $C$-orbit ($p$ cells) checking equality; abort the subgroup at the first failing orbit. Report ``symmetric'' at the first subgroup all of whose orbits pass; report ``asymmetric'' if all subgroups fail.

lean.text:
| e :: rest =>
      let t := subgroupTest stopEarly s (ord e) e.1 e.2
      if t.1 then (true, t.2.2)
      else
        let r := detect stopEarly s ord rest
        (r.1, t.2.2 + r.2)

maps.note: `detect stopEarly s ord sched` runs the subgroup tests in schedule order and returns (verdict, total cells read). It is a Lean function, so the read count is computed, not postulated.
